chunks: From him, from Ubdous ibn Ibrahim al-Baghdadi, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: 'Henna removes the odour, increases the moisture of the face, aromatises the breath, and improves the offspring.'

key_terms.النَّكْهَةَ: Breath or scent of the mouth
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءُ: Henna (the plant/paste used for dyeing and adornment)

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of using henna according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the practical wisdom of henna (*al-hinna*) in maintaining personal hygiene and aesthetic beauty, which are highly valued in Shia tradition as acts of self-care and preparation for worship. The narration specifically notes its efficacy in removing body odor (*al-sahak*), enhancing facial moisture, improving breath scent, and positively influencing the quality of offspring, reflecting the holistic view of physical well-being in Islamic teachings.
